newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Cruz Blanca to boost capital.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Cruz Blanca to boost capital.

text.p: Chilean insurance company Cruz Blanca Prevision y Seguros SA approved Friday a capital increase of 24.7 billion pesos, or about $57 million, to finance its purchase of a stake in competitor Consorcio Nacional de Seguros, the company said.
The capital boost, approved by shareholders at an extraordinary meeting, will be through new shares offered preferentially to current holders in three stages, said General Manager Fabio Valdes.

The money will go towards Cruz Blanca's previously announced purchase of a share of Consorcio Nacional for $109 million, with the balance of the purchase money coming from sale of international assets for about $60 million, officials said.
At the end of the capital increase, all the new shares are expected to be held by current stockholders, said company president Hernan Buchi.

Cruz Blanca, Bankers Trust New York Corp and Banmedica SA teamed up for a strategic alliance on June 12 to buy Consorcio Nacional, giving the U.S. company a major presence in the Chilean insurance and annuity business.

Under the deal, each of the purchasers will pay Bankers Trust $109 million for 25 percent stakes in Consorcio Nacional, with Bankers Trust holding 50 percent of the company after the separate transactions. Santiago-based Consorcio Nacional is Chile's largest insurance and annuities firm.
